newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close mixed in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close mixed in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed mixed in lackluster trade, brokers said, with little expectation that activity will grow before the end of the year.
"It was a slow, thin market and there's little immediate prospect of it improving," said Cavelba broker Eduardo Blanco.
"Not even tariff rises for CANTV or news of a share dividend for Electricidad de Caracas have boosted the bolsa," he added.
The index closed up 0.28 percent at 6,131.72 points as 21 shares fell, 16 rose and five closed flat, according to preliminary figures from the stock exchange.
Telephone company CANTV closed up 4.00 bolivars at 1799.00. Electricidad de Caracas, which said last week it would reinstate dividend payments, slipped 3.00 bolivars to 521.00.

Trade volume was boosted to 24.7 million shares, worth 2 billion bolivars ($4.3 million), as 3.1 million shares in food company Mavesa traded and 10.7 million B shares in paints company Corimon. Mavesa, which announced it would invest $12 million in a new cleaning products factory, closed up 0.50 bolivars at 136.00, while Corimon B shares slipped 0.75 bolivars to 7.75.
